title: Infra: GPU fleet, Cloud Accounts, IaC modules & CI/CD - Consolidated Runbook
author: Leah M. Carter
content:
Summary

This consolidated runbook documents operational standards, IaC modules, CI/CD build practices, cloud account and networking guardrails, and GPU fleet capacity planning used by the Infra team. It is intended as the single reference for day-1 provisioning, day-2 operations, incident response, and ongoing capacity tuning for GPU-backed inference services.

Scope

- GPU fleet lifecycle (node image, onboarding, decommission)
- Capacity planning and autoscaling policy thresholds
- Cloud accounts and network baseline for private & dedicated deployments
- Terraform modules and versioning guidelines
- CI/CD pipelines for image build, IaC plan/apply, and service deploys
- Runbook steps for common incidents and rollbacks

Owner & Roster

- Primary owner: Infra - GPU Fleet (oncall rotation)
- Secondary owner: Infra - Cloud Accounts & Networking
- Pager contacts: infra-oncall@redwood.internal, infra-leads@redwood.internal
- SRE escalation: pager -> Slack #infra-escalations -> Engineering Director (on-call)

Architecture & Key Services

- fleet-manager: central controller that maintains desired node counts and placements. Responsible for TTLs, health checks, and drain/cordon operations.
- gpu-orchestrator: autoscaler that reacts to queue depth and per-GPU utilization metrics.
- image-builder: CI job that builds GPU node images (OS + runtime + drivers + agent).
- cloud-accounts-guardian: service that validates account-level constraints (VPCs, IAM, tagging) during provisioning.
- telemetry-bridge: forwards GPU metrics and allocation events to Datadog/Prometheus and billing-bridge for cost attribution.

Capacity planning & SLOs

Goals (production inference clusters):
- 95th percentile GPU allocation latency < 30s
- Node creation time (bootstrap + join) < 6 minutes
- Node preempt/termination recovery complete < 4 minutes
- Target cluster average GPU utilization 65-85%
- Reserve buffer: 10% spare GPUs for emergency capacity and burst workloads

Autoscaling thresholds (recommended baseline):
- Scale-up when: average queue_depth_per_cluster > 200 OR avg_gpu_utilization > 80% for 5m
- Scale-down when: avg_gpu_utilization < 55% for 10m AND queue_depth_per_cluster < 50
- Safety caps: max_scale_step = 25% of current capacity, min_free_gpu_pool = ceil(0.10 * desired_capacity)

Capacity review cadence:
1) Weekly dashboard review (SRE + Infra) - utilization, burn-rate, node error rates
2) Monthly forecast update with Sales/Customer Success for Dedicated contracts
3) Quarterly topology review (regions, AZ skew, instance families)

Cloud Accounts & Networking Checklist (bootstrap)

When creating a new cloud account for GPUs (AWS / GCP / Azure):
- Create restricted admin IAM role: infra-admin-<env> (least privilege for provisioning)
- VPC design: at least 3 AZ subnets, private subnets for GPU nodes, NAT gateways in each AZ
- Security groups: GPU nodes allow egress and only control-plane inbound from management CIDRs
- Tagging policy: team, env, cost-center, project, owner (required for all resources)
- Service limits: request GPU quota increase proactively (include expected sustained vGPU count)
- Networking: set MTU to 9001 for high-throughput RDMA-enabled instances where applicable
- NACLs and flow logs enabled for troubleshooting

Terraform / IaC modules & versioning

Module policy:
- Modules must be idempotent and include automated unit tests (terratest or kitchen-terraform)
- Semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Infra changes that touch runtime defaults require MINOR bump; behavioral changes to scale logic require MAJOR bump.
- All modules must include a README with inputs, outputs, example usage, and ownership.

Key modules (examples):
- module/gpu-node (v1.4.2): provisions GPU node ASG/instance template, userdata to join fleet, driver install steps.
- module/gpu-k8s-nodegroup (v2.1.0): Kubernetes nodegroup resources, taints/tolerations, labels for scheduling.
- module/vpc-baseline (v3.0.1): shared VPC with subnetting & routing, flow logs toggle.
- module/cloud-accounts-bootstrap (v1.2.0): IAM roles, organizations, SCP attachments, service-quotas requests automation.
- module/monitoring-agent (v1.0.3): installs telemetry agent and configures Datadog metrics/trace forwarding.

Example Terraform snippet

module "gpu_node" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@stash.redwood.internal/infra/terraform-modules.git//module/gpu-node?ref=v1.4.2"
  env = "prod"
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  ssh_keys = ["infra-deploy-key"]
}

CI/CD & Build pipelines

Pipeline responsibilities:
- image-build-pipeline: builds and tests node images, publishes AMIs/container images with semantic tags.
- iac-plan-and-apply: runs terraform fmt/validate/plan in PRs; apply runs only from release pipeline with manual approvals for prod.
- service-deploy: performs canary deploys for fleet-manager and gpu-orchestrator services with automated smoke tests.

Recommended pipeline steps (image-build-pipeline):
1) Checkout + lint + unit tests
2) Build image (packer/docker build)
3) Run integration smoke tests in ephemeral cluster (minimum: driver load, agent heartbeat, kube join)
4) Publish artifact to registry/AMI catalog with tag: <module>-v<semver>-<date>
5) Trigger iac-plan job to update cluster launch template if image changes.

IaC PR workflow:
- All terraform changes require at least one peer review and one approver from infra-owners team.
- CI enforces terraform fmt, static analysis, and runs plan. Plan artifacts are posted to PR.
- Prod applies require a two-step approval: infra-release and platform-security.

Runbooks (common playbooks)

1) GPU node failing health checks (symptom: node in NotReady / kubelet crashloop)
- Step 1: Identify node: kubectl get nodes -l gpu-node=true -o wide; check node age and recent events.
- Step 2: Inspect agent and kernel logs: ssh -> sudo journalctl -u gpu-agent -n 500; check dmesg for OOM or driver faults.
- Step 3: If transient, cordon and drain then reboot: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; reboot node.
- Step 4: If persistent driver error, mark node for rebuild: tag instance as rebuild-needed and trigger image-builder pipeline.
- Step 5: Postmortem: if >5% of cluster nodes impacted, open postmortem and escalate to Infra Leads.

2) Unplanned capacity shortfall (symptom: allocation latency spike > SLO)
- Step 1: Validate metrics: check queue depth, allocation latency, pending pods.
- Step 2: Temporarily raise max scale step and increase desired_capacity manually in fleet-manager UI or via terraform force scale input.
- Step 3: If cloud quota hit, open emergency quota request with cloud-provider and temporarily route traffic to alternate region.
- Step 4: After recovery, run capacity analysis and create action items (increase baseline, change scaling policy, or purchase Reserved/Committed capacity).

3) CI/CD image regression (symptom: new image causing higher node join failures)
- Step 1: Rollback: revert to previous image tag via iac pipeline and trigger apply with manual approval.
- Step 2: Quarantine faulty image in artifact registry and re-run image-build pipeline with stricter smoke tests.
- Step 3: Notify SRE and CS if customer SLA impacted.

Operational dashboards & alerts

- Dashboards: GPU Fleet Overview (utilization, allocation latency, node state distribution), Node Health (driver errors, kernel OOMs), Cost & Burn (cost per GPU-hour by region).
- Alerts (examples):
  - allocation_latency.p95 > 45s for 5m -> severity P1
  - node_boot_time > 7m for 3 nodes in a row -> severity P2
  - driver_install_fail_rate > 3% in 30m -> severity P2

Change & Release Guidelines

- All infra changes that affect capacity behavior (scaling algorithms, thresholds, image defaults) must be:
  1) Code-reviewed
  2) Tested in staging cluster with representative workload
  3) Announced on #infra-changes with a 48-hour review window for major changes
  4) Deployed via canary with automated rollback on increased error rate or allocation latency regressions

Post-Incident Review (PIR) Checklist

- Time-window: create PIR within 72 hours for P1/P0 incidents.
- Include: timeline, impact, root cause analysis, contributing factors, action items with owners and ETA.
- Track action items in central board and verify closure at monthly reliability review.

Appendix: Example CLI commands and helpful snippets

- Force scale fleet-manager (terraform approach):
# Increase desired count by 20% (example)
terraform workspace select prod
terraform apply -var 'fleet_desired_count=150' -auto-approve

- Quick node inspection:
kubectl describe node <node-name>
journalctl -u gpu-agent -n 200
sudo cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log

- Create quota request template (GCP):
project: redwood-prod-<region>
quota: GCE_GPU_ALL_REGIONS
requested_increase: 200
justification: Sustained inference capacity for dedicated customer commitments

References & Related Docs

- infra-gpu-fleet-capacity-iac-ci-cd-networking-runbook-2026.json (capacity playbook)
- infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026.json (IaC module details and onboarding checklist)
- gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026.json (day-to-day runbook)

Document maintenance

- Responsible owner must review this doc quarterly or after any P1 incident and update module versions and thresholds.

End of document
